body.statement: As a corollary of observed-law coverage and the inversion definitions, \(q\in R_n\) implies \(S(q)\subseteq C_n\) and \(S(q)\in\mathcal H_n\). Therefore, for every \(n\) and every compatible law, \[\Pr_q\{S(q)\subseteq C_n\}\ge1-\alpha,\qquad \Pr_q\{S(q)\in\mathcal H_n\}\ge1-\alpha.\] These inclusions remain valid on structural-zero faces, when an instrument arm has zero sample count, and when empirical cell differences are incompatible with monotonicity.
body.justification: The corollary records the finite-sample honesty inherited directly from simultaneous multinomial coverage.
body.gap: Romano--Shaikh supplies the general inversion logic; the corollary specializes it to the common-rank path correspondence and its set-of-sets image.
body.consumer: Policy analysts retain finite-sample-valid outer conclusions wherever local Gaussian calibration is uncertified.
